steps.question: Which genes differ between the 6 treated samples (batch B2) and the 6 control samples (batch B1), under the explicit assumption of no batch effect, with every result labeled as confounded?

grounding.reason: Two-group count comparison, 6 vs 6 raw salmon gene counts, flagged by R-0005@668f: batch perfectly confounded with condition; the chosen side is to proceed under the stated no-batch-effect assumption with every result labeled confounded, not to stop.

constraints: Do NOT include batch in the design formula and do NOT apply ComBat-seq, removeBatchEffect, or any surrogate-variable method: batch is perfectly confounded with condition, the model matrix would not be full rank, and a removal method would remove the condition effect with the batch (R-0005@668f). Proceed under the explicitly stated assumption of no batch effect and label every result as confounded (flag outcome confounded_label_or_stop).

Fit the counts AS DELIVERED with no length offset: the input is a gene-level table from salmon with no per-sample quantification files and no average-transcript-length table, so tximport must NOT be run on it and no length input may be invented; state in the report that the length offset is lost and that altered isoform use can appear as differential expression (R-0169@18ab).
Do not scale, transform, or pre-normalize the counts; DESeq2 median-of-ratios size factors are the normalization, applied as an offset inside the model (R-0026@9ab1).

Pre-filter minimally: keep genes with at least 10 counts in at least the smallest group size (6 samples); the independent filter in results() does the rest (R-0002@087b, R-0029@22ca, doi:10.1073/pnas.0914005107).

Set the condition factor reference level explicitly to control before the model; name the contrast as factor/numerator/denominator (condition, treated, control) so a positive log2FoldChange means higher in treated (R-0036@e6d8 logic, vignette:DESeq2/1.52.0#note-on-factor-levels).
Test: DESeq2 Wald test; keep Cook's-distance outlier flagging on (6 replicates per group < 7, so flagged genes get NA p-values — count and report them, do not silently drop) (R-0039@968d).
Shrinkage: lfcShrink with apeglm on the treated-vs-control coefficient; keep the unshrunken estimate and its SE beside the shrunken one; p-values come from the unshrunken fit (R-0009@310d).

Multiple testing: keep results() independent filtering ON, pass alpha = 0.05 to results(), adjust with BH, select by padj < 0.05 only — never by unadjusted p-value or by fold change alone (R-0166@bbcd, R-0010@6072, R-0043@4f55).

Robustness at 6 replicates per group: also run edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test (TMM normalization, glmQLFit, glmQLFTest) on the same counts and same condition-only design, and report the overlap with the DESeq2 calls; treat the intersection as the high-confidence set (R-0042@54e1, R-0001@9a17).
Inspect the p-value histogram of unadjusted p-values before interpreting adjusted values and report its shape (R-0083@12de).
Do not use Harmony or any embedding-based correction: it is a single-cell method and gives no testable bulk input (R-0149@aa57).

plan.title: Treated vs control DE, batch-confounded (labeled)
plan.analytical_narrative: The research question is 'Which genes differ between treated and control?' in a human lung bulk RNA-seq dataset of 6 treated vs 6 control samples (12,000 genes, salmon-derived gene counts). The critical design fact is that processing batch is perfectly confounded with condition: batch B1 holds all controls and batch B2 holds all treated samples. Per rule R-0005@668f, no batch term can be fitted and no batch-removal method (ComBat-seq, removeBatchEffect, surrogate variables) may be applied — the design matrix would not be full rank and any removal method would remove the condition effect with the batch. The permitted route is to state the assumption of no batch effect, run the standard two-group count model on the counts as delivered, and label every result as confounded. The plan therefore: (1) runs sample-structure QC first — blind variance-stabilizing transform, PCA on the 500 most variable genes, and a sample-distance heatmap, each colored by condition and by batch, so the reader sees that condition and batch axes coincide; (2) fits the DESeq2 negative binomial Wald test on a condition-only design with median-of-ratios size factors, a minimal pre-filter (10 counts in at least 6 samples), apeglm-shrunken log2 fold changes, BH adjustment at alpha 0.05 with independent filtering, plus an edgeR quasi-likelihood run on the same counts for robustness (6 replicates per group is at the low end); (3) reports the gene table with both unshrunken and shrunken fold changes, MA and dispersion diagnostics, the p-value histogram, the DESeq2/edgeR overlap, and an explicit confounded-design limitation. Because the counts come from salmon as a gene-level table with no per-sample quantification files or transcript-length table, the length offset is lost; the model is fitted without a length offset and the report states that a change in isoform use can appear as differential expression.

flags.message: A quantifier name alone does not establish that the length correction occurred. If the counts come from Salmon, kallisto, or RSEM as a gene-level table, with no per-sample quantification files and no average transcript length table, the import state is not established. Ask for the per-sample quantification files, quant.sf, abundance.h5, or genes.results, or for the average transcript length table per gene and sample. If neither arrives, fit the count model on the counts as delivered, with no length offset, and state in the plan and in the report that the length offset is lost and that a change in isoform use can show as differential expression. Do not run tximport on a gene table, because tximport imports transcript estimates, and do not invent a length input.

If the batch is perfectly confounded with the condition, do not fit a batch term and do not adjust the counts with ComBat-seq, removeBatchEffect, or a surrogate variable method. The model matrix is not full rank, and a removal method would remove the condition effect with the batch. State the assumption of no batch effect and label every result as confounded, or stop and ask for a design where the batches hold every condition.
